name: Oxymetholone

card.summary: Anadrol: an anemia drug that bodybuilders use as a potent oral bulker, with a well-documented liver-toxicity profile and almost no physique trials.
card.note: 17-alpha-alkylated oral steroid; hepatotoxicity (peliosis hepatis, liver tumours) is documented in medical use.

quick.overview:
Oxymetholone, sold as Anadrol, is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid approved in some countries for anemias caused by bone-marrow failure. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a strong oral for mass and fullness, and some users pair it with injectable testosterone in cycles.

The published research is about its medical use, not its effect on appearance. Hematology reviews describe it, with danazol, as one of the androgens commonly used in inherited marrow failure, and a general-purpose reference text describes lean-mass gains in short-term wasting studies.
quick.mechanism: It is a 17-alpha-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone that activates the androgen receptor and also stimulates red-cell production. The alkylation permits oral use but is associated with liver stress.[1][2]
quick.risks: Reviews of androgen therapy for marrow failure report virilization and liver toxicity as major adverse events, and case series link oral androgens to peliosis hepatis and liver tumours.[2][3][4] Forum users also discuss unfavourable cholesterol effects and gynecomastia.[5][6] It is a controlled substance in many places and banned in sport.

lead: Oxymetholone, sold as Anadrol and Anapolon, is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid approved for anemias caused by deficient red-cell production. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a strong oral for adding muscle mass and fullness, giving a bigger, more masculine frame, often in cycles with injectable testosterone.[27][8][10]

Syntex scientists first described it in 1959, and it reached the market in the early 1960s.[27] Trials have studied it in marrow failure, dialysis anemia and HIV wasting; the 2003 phase III HIV-wasting trial found significant weight and body-cell-mass gains over placebo alongside liver-enzyme elevations.[28] Reviews identify liver toxicity and virilization as its major adverse events, and it is a Schedule III controlled substance in the United States.[2][29][27]
infobox: Schedule III in the US; controlled in many countries; prohibited in sport[27][31]
Trials in HIV wasting and dialysis; none in healthy lifters[28]

paras: Oxymetholone is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) that clinicians prescribe for certain anemias and that bodybuilders and appearance-focused users take for muscle size and a fuller, more muscular look. Wikipedia describes it as highly effective at promoting gains in body mass in non-medical users, and in the United States anemia is its only remaining approved indication.[27] Its look-related appeal is mass: more fat-free tissue and water-filled fullness on the frame, which is how forum users describe the physique change.

Oxymetholone has been used as an androgen therapy for bone-marrow failure. A hematology review states that androgens are the main non-transplant therapy for marrow failure in dyskeratosis congenita and Fanconi anemia, reporting responses in up to 80 percent of cases, with danazol and oxymetholone the most commonly used and virilization and liver toxicity the major adverse events.[2] A review of androgen therapy in aplastic anaemia noted that earlier reports of response rates comparable to marrow transplantation had given way to markedly lower recovery rates in later reports, possibly reflecting differences in supportive care and in evaluation of residual marrow function.[7] Small clinical studies of oxymetholone in bone-marrow insufficiency date to the 1970s.[14]

Androgens including oxymetholone were tested for anemia in dialysis patients, and a Cochrane review examined androgen therapy for the anemia of chronic kidney disease in adults.[13][15] A controlled trial found that nandrolone decanoate and oxymetholone did not protect the bone marrow from suppression during methotrexate chemotherapy.[16] Wikipedia lists osteoporosis, HIV/AIDS wasting and weight gain in some patients among other uses that have been tried, and the 2001 Clinical Therapeutics review mentions studies in antithrombin III deficiency, paediatric growth impairment and damaged myocardium with varying success.[27][29]

Users on looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums consider oxymetholone for muscle mass and for a masculinised physique and face. A post from a user in Argentina asked whether oxymetholone or stanozolol would be more useful to masculinise the face and physique, and others asked which oral to add to a stack for mass or to escape a skinny-fat look.[9][10] Another thread asks which SERM to pair with oxymetholone, and a teenager's posted plan describes adding it to a testosterone-based stack alongside other compounds.[17][8] These are user reports; no controlled trial has assessed such outcomes in healthy lifters.
Among non-medical users, Wikipedia notes that anabolic steroids as a class are used mostly by men who are not competitive athletes and who take them for appearance.[31]

Trials of oxymetholone concern medical conditions. A 1974 trial examined bone-marrow insufficiency, a controlled trial found no marrow protection during methotrexate chemotherapy, a randomised comparison tested androgens for anemia in hemodialysis patients, and a Cochrane review of androgens for anemia of chronic kidney disease covered eight studies and 181 participants.[14][16][13][15]

The largest body-composition trial is a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled phase III study of 89 HIV-positive women and men with wasting, published in AIDS in 2003. Participants received oxymetholone on one of two daily schedules or placebo for 16 weeks. Weight rose by 3.0 to 3.5 kg on oxymetholone versus 1.0 kg on placebo, and body cell mass rose by 3.8 kg in the twice-daily group (12.4 percent of baseline). Appetite and well-being improved. Liver toxicity was the main adverse event: ALT rose more than five-fold above baseline in 27 to 35 percent of treated patients and in none on placebo.[28]

Two double-blind trials in Thai dialysis patients by Aramwit and colleagues reported body-composition changes. In 44 haemodialysis patients over 24 weeks, fat-free mass rose by 3.24 kg on oxymetholone versus 0.65 kg on placebo, with elevated liver enzymes in two treated patients; the paper reported improved insulin sensitivity.[33] In 24 peritoneal-dialysis patients also receiving erythropoietin, six months of oxymetholone raised haemoglobin and hematocrit and increased weight and lean body mass versus placebo, with liver-enzyme rises as the main side effect.[34]
These studies enrolled patients with wasting or kidney failure, not healthy people training for physique. No published trial has tested oxymetholone for physique or facial outcomes in healthy people.

The medical literature on androgen therapy identifies virilization and liver toxicity as major adverse events.[2] The 2001 Clinical Therapeutics review calls liver toxicity, especially cholestatic jaundice, the major adverse effect, with peliosis hepatis and liver tumours less common, and lists acne, hirsutism, hair loss, voice changes, gynecomastia and changes in libido among androgenic effects of AAS in general.[29] Wikipedia lists acne, hair growth, voice changes, depression, headache, fluid retention and, rarely, gynecomastia, and notes that periodic liver function tests are recommended because of its 17-alpha-alkylated structure.[27]

A review of androgens and liver tumours reported that the association between anabolic androgenic steroids and hepatic tumours was first noted in patients with Fanconi anemia, and examined whether non-Fanconi patients and those given parenteral androgens are also at risk.[4] A series of twelve cases of peliosis hepatis was reported in association with oral androgen therapy.[3] A case report and review in the British Journal of Sports Medicine described hepatocellular adenomas in two bodybuilders who used AAS; the tumours tended to shrink after use stopped, and the authors suggested ultrasound monitoring for athletes using AAS.[32] The U.S. Report on Carcinogens includes a profile of oxymetholone.[18]

Beyond the liver, Wikipedia's anabolic steroid article describes lower HDL and higher LDL cholesterol, raised blood pressure, suppressed natural testosterone and fertility, and, in adolescents, possible early growth-plate closure, as effects of AAS as a class.[31] A review of supraphysiologic-dose AAS use proposed it may be a risk factor for dementia, addressing AAS generally rather than oxymetholone specifically.[19] A rat study of four anabolic steroids, including oxymetholone, found increased dopaminergic and serotonergic activity in brain regions after long-term treatment.[20]

T Nation contributors note that orals such as oxymetholone depress HDL cholesterol and raise LDL more than injectables, that gynecomastia can occur early, and that oxymetholone has been called harsh, though one poster argued that dose is the relevant factor.[5][12][6] A thread on kidney effects also circulated binding-affinity data for oxymetholone.[21]

Oxymetholone is an androgen-receptor agonist with strong anabolic and weak androgenic activity, and it also stimulates red-cell production, possibly via erythropoietin and effects on marrow progenitors.[27][1] Relative-binding studies of anabolic steroids found that some compounds, among them oxymetholone, bound the androgen receptor too weakly to measure, a point noted in forum discussions of how it acts.[21][22]

A review by Kicman discusses how androgen-receptor expression, steroid metabolism and coactivator interactions may explain why some steroids separate anabolic from androgenic effects, and cautions that the benefit of anabolic steroids for physical function and quality of life in clinical settings is still being established.[30]

Oxymetholone is a 17-alpha-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone; its chemical name is 17beta-hydroxy-2-(hydroxymethylene)-17-methyl-5alpha-androstan-3-one.[29] The alkyl group lets it survive first-pass liver metabolism so it can be taken by mouth, and is associated with its hepatotoxicity.[27][31] It is well absorbed orally, metabolised in the liver and excreted in urine; pharmacokinetic data are limited and its elimination half-life is unknown.[27] The 2001 review notes it had few pharmacokinetic or tolerability studies before approval in the 1960s.[29]

Syntex scientists first described oxymetholone in 1959, and it was marketed in the United Kingdom as Anapolon and in the United States in the early 1960s, with Anadrol the best-known American brand name.[27][29] Its use in marrow failure and anemia grew through the 1960s and 1970s, and trials in HIV wasting followed in the 2000s.[14][28] Today it is best known outside medicine as an oral bulking compound in bodybuilding culture.

Oxymetholone is a Schedule III controlled substance in the United States, and many other countries also control anabolic steroids, which makes non-medical use generally illicit; a black market of smuggled, underground and counterfeit products exists where they are controlled.[27][31] Most major sporting bodies ban anabolic steroids, and anti-doping research has studied oxymetholone metabolites in urine.[31]

subs.h: Use in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities
paras: On T Nation, users discuss oxymetholone as a medically indicated drug for anemias and wasting that is not appropriate to take for bodybuilding, and as one of the substances on lists of prohibited anabolic agents for natural contests.[23][24] Forum threads treat it as part of oral stacks, and members debate low-dose versus higher-dose approaches.[25][12] On looksmax.org, threads compare it with other orals for mass and ask about pairing it with SERMs, reflecting a wider culture in which steroid use is discussed as a route to a more muscular, masculine look.[8][9][10][17]

timeline.event: Marketed as Anapolon in the UK and Anadrol in the US; approved for anemias from deficient red-cell production.[27][29]
Clinical study of oxymetholone therapy in bone-marrow insufficiency published.[14]
Case series links oral androgens, including oxymetholone, with peliosis hepatis.[3]
Pavlatos and colleagues publish a Clinical Therapeutics review of oxymetholone.[29]
Phase III placebo-controlled trial in HIV wasting reports weight and body cell mass gains and liver-enzyme rises.[28]
Review of androgens and liver tumours in Fanconi anemia and non-Fanconi conditions.[4]
Randomised trial in hemodialysis patients reports fat-free mass gains.[33]
Trial in peritoneal-dialysis patients reports hematologic and lean-mass changes.[34]

lore.intro: Oxymetholone is discussed on looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums as a strong oral for mass; users trade cycle plans while others point to cholesterol and liver effects.[8][10][5]

claims.claim: Anadrol is a powerful oral for fast mass and fullness.
claims.believers: Forum users list it with other orals as an option to add to a stack to escape a skinny-fat look.[10][11]
claims.experts: The published trials concern anemia and wasting; in HIV wasting, oxymetholone increased weight and body cell mass versus placebo, and no trial has measured physique outcomes in healthy people.[2][13][28]

claims.claim: Anadrol can masculinise the face and body.
claims.believers: A forum poster asked whether it would be more useful than stanozolol for masculinising face and physique.[9]
claims.experts: No published study has examined facial or aesthetic effects of oxymetholone; clinical reviews report virilization as an adverse effect in patients.[2]

claims.claim: Its reputation for harshness is overstated at low doses.
claims.believers: One T Nation poster argued the drug's reputation depends on dose and that results can be obtained at lower amounts.[25][12]
claims.experts: Reviews list liver toxicity as a major adverse event, a phase III trial recorded ALT rises in treated patients, and case series link oral androgens with peliosis hepatis and liver tumours.[2][3][4][28]

claims.claim: Orals like oxymetholone damage cholesterol far more than injectables.
claims.believers: T Nation posters state that it crushes HDL and raises LDL more than injectable compounds.[5]
claims.experts: No dedicated published lipid trial of oxymetholone was located; forum posters cite general literature on androgen-induced dyslipidemia.[26]

claims.claim: Anadrol adds size mostly as water and bloat.
claims.believers: Forum users describe fullness and rapid scale weight gain and debate how much is fluid; low-dose users say they avoid the puffy look.[25][12]
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists fluid retention among side effects, and trials in wasting report gains in lean mass or body cell mass measured by bioimpedance.[27][28]

claims.claim: A liver 'protectant' or monitoring makes orals safe.
claims.believers: Posters recommend supplements and bloodwork alongside orals.[5]
claims.experts: Reviews recommend periodic liver tests with oxymetholone, and case reports describe adenomas in bodybuilders that shrank after AAS use stopped.[27][32]

claims.claim: It is a medical drug, not a bodybuilding drug.
claims.believers: Some T Nation contributors say it belongs to patients with anemia or wasting.[23]
claims.experts: It is approved in the US for anemias; non-medical use is illicit under Schedule III controls.[27]
